comment: Read by scripts/third-party-notices.mjs. 'copyright': crates for which no licence file with a real copyright notice exists in the crate or its repository. Their text is the licence template of cargo-about with the placeholder replaced by 'holder'. basis 'authors': holder is the authors field of the crate (checked against cargo metadata at the exact version). basis 'repository': holder named from the upstream repository, see 'source'. An entry is used only for the exact name and version, and an entry that is no longer needed is an error. 'fontLicenseFile': the licence of the Inter font that the web vault embeds. 'vendored': third-party files that the web vault ships from web/vendor (the list must agree with web/vendor/MANIFEST.json; each entry names the licence file and says what Faithful Ferret changed).
intro: The Rust crates are those that two programs are built from: the server binary (the static
Linux builds for x86_64 and aarch64 that the Docker image contains) and the WebAssembly
module of the crypto core (the release archives ferret-core-wasm-web and ferret-core-wasm-node,
and the copy of the module that the web vault in the server image embeds). A crate that only
runs while the program is built (a build script) is not listed. A crate that is only used at
build time through a procedural macro may be listed. The Docker image carries this whole file;
each release archive carries it too.
The web vault has no runtime npm packages. It embeds a Latin subset of the Inter font and one
file from another project, the QR code generator of Project Nayuki; both are listed after the
Rust crates. The container image is based on Alpine Linux; the packages that Alpine installs
keep their own licence information in the image (/lib/apk/db/installed).
